name: japanlaw
description: Japanese law, answered from the statute itself: the Japanese as published, the Ministry of Justice's English where there is one and marked machine translation where there is not, every provision quoted with its link. Read-only tools from japanlaw.org's MCP server, and a skill that teaches how a Japanese provision is cited and which English may be quoted.

interface.longDescription:
Japanese law, answered from the statute itself: the Japanese as published, the Ministry of Justice's English where there is one and marked machine translation where there is not, every provision quoted with its link. Read-only tools from japanlaw.org's MCP server, and a skill that teaches how a Japanese provision is cited and which English may be quoted.

For anyone who has to deal with a Japanese law: a worker, an employer, someone new to Japan, a lawyer abroad. Ask what an article says, what a word in a law means, or what an amendment changed, and the answer quotes the provision, links its page on japanlaw.org, and says whose English it is.

No account, no key and nothing to configure. What you ask is not recorded. It is information about the law, not legal advice.
capabilities: Read a provision or a law
Look up the words a law defines
defaultPrompt: Under Japanese law, how many hours of overtime can my employer ask of me in a month? Quote the article.
What does Article 36 of the Labor Standards Act say? Show the Japanese and say whose English it is.
I'm renting an apartment in Tokyo. When can the landlord refuse to renew the lease?
